extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners and patent applicants/agents (practitioners) working with RCEs and after-final/transitional practice
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for filing, processing, and evaluating Requests for Continued Examination (RCEs) under 37 CFR 1.114 and transitional after-final submissions under 37 CFR 1.129(a), including what counts as a submission, eligibility, processing checks, and treatment of improper or nonresponsive submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of timely payment under 37 CFR 1.17(r) for 37 CFR 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(r) is timely paid in connection with a submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a), the finality of the previous Office action is withdrawn automatically and the submission will be entered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'conditional' payment (authorization to charge deposit account/credit card if not otherwise entered) is treated as an unconditional payment. If a Notice of Appeal and appeal fee were filed prior to or with the payment, payment is construed as a request to dismiss the appeal and continue prosecution under 37 CFR 1.129(a). Use form paragraph 7.42.01.fti to notify applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonresponsive submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) — two-month shortened period
rubrics_metrics.description: If a submission under 37 CFR 1.129(a) is not fully responsive to the prior Office action (e.g., only an IDS), applicant is given a shortened statutory period of TWO MONTHS to submit a complete reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the submission appears to be a bona fide attempt to reply but is not fully responsive, use form paragraph 7.42.02.fti to notify applicant and set the two-month period. If an appeal was filed before payment, payment is construed as request to dismiss the appeal; the appeal stands dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of first Office action following pre-June 8, 2005 submissions under 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: For submissions under 37 CFR 1.129(a) filed prior to June 8, 2005, after submission and payment of the 1.17(r) fee, the next Office action on the merits may be made final only under the conditions for making a first action in a continuing application final set forth in MPEP § 706.07(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.42.03.fti may be used where appropriate to make the first action final following such a submission. A shortened statutory period and extension rules apply as described in MPEP § 706.07(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of Office action following 1.129(a) submissions on/after June 8, 2005
rubrics_metrics.description: For submissions under 37 CFR 1.129(a) filed on or after June 8, 2005, the next Office action following the submission will be equivalent to the next Office action after a reply to a non-final Office action and will be made final except where the examiner introduces a new ground of rejection not necessitated by applicant’s amendment or not based on IDS information filed under 37 CFR 1.97(c) with the 1.17(p) fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 706.07(a). Use form paragraph 7.42.031.fti to make such an action final when appropriate. A three-month shortened statutory period for reply applies; special rules if a first reply is filed within two months and advisory action timing may extend the three-month period, but reply period will never be later than six months from mailing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on number of after-final submissions under transitional 37 CFR 1.129(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants eligible for the transitional limited examination procedure under 37 CFR 1.129(a) are entitled to consideration of two after-final submissions only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fee under 1.17(r) has been twice paid, 1.129(a) provisions are no longer available. Additional submissions may be considered only under current after-final practice (37 CFR 1.116). Use form paragraph 7.41.02.fti for second-submission matters and follow restrictions on introducing new matter (35 U.S.C. 132).

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE available only when prosecution is closed and before certain events (37 CFR 1.114(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may request continued examination (RCE) by filing a submission and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e) prior to the earliest of: (1) payment of the issue fee (unless a petition under 1.313 is granted), (2) abandonment, or (3) filing of a notice of appeal to the CAFC or commencement of certain civil actions (unless terminated).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prosecution is 'closed' if the application is under appeal, or the last Office action is final, a notice of allowance, or another action that otherwise closes prosecution (e.g., Ex parte Quayle). See 37 CFR 1.114(a)-(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of submission for RCE (37 CFR 1.114(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'submission' includes, but is not limited to, an information disclosure statement, an amendment to the written description, claims, or drawings, new arguments, or new evidence in support of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If reply to an Office action under 35 U.S.C. 132 is outstanding, the submission must meet the reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111. Previously filed amendments after final (entered or unentered) or arguments from appeal briefs may satisfy the submission requirement where responsive within 37 CFR 1.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of timely RCE filing and fee payment
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant timely files a submission and the fee set forth in 37 CFR 1.17(e), the Office will withdraw the finality of any Office action to which a reply is outstanding and the submission will be entered and considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing an RCE after appeal but prior to decision will be treated as request to withdraw appeal and reopen prosecution. Appeal or reply briefs and related papers are not themselves submissions under 1.114 unless incorporated or made responsive under 1.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE cannot be used to switch inventions (37 CFR 1.145)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants cannot obtain continued examination via an RCE for claims that are independent and distinct from the claims previously claimed and examined as a matter of right (i.e., cannot switch inventions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any newly submitted claims directed to an independent and distinct invention will be withdrawn from consideration and not entered. RCE is not a new application and will not be converted to a continuing application or CPA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility limitations for RCE (37 CFR 1.114(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.114 provisions apply to utility or plant applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or international applications filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995; RCE provisions do not apply to provisional applications, utility/plant applications filed before June 8, 1995, certain international applications, design applications, international design applications, or patents under reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For national stage RCEs, all required inventor oaths/declarations (or substitute statements) must be submitted prior to or with the RCE per 35 U.S.C. 371(c)(4) and 37 CFR 1.495(c)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing checklist for RCEs (TC verification items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical support personnel must verify: (A) application is utility/plant (not design), (B) application filed on/after June 8, 1995, (C) prosecution is closed, (D) RCE filed before issue fee payment or petition granted, (E) application pending when RCE filed, (F) RCE accompanied by proper fee(s) including 1.17(e), (G) RCE included a submission as required by 1.114, and (H) for national stage, compliant inventor’s oath/declaration submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An RCE will not be processed if the application is undergoing court review at the Federal Circuit or district court because the application is in the court's jurisdiction and RCE procedure is not available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of improper RCE — notice and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If one or more conditions for filing an RCE are not satisfied, applicant will be notified (generally via Form PTO-2051 'Notice of Improper Request for Continued Examination (RCE)'). An improper RCE will not toll any time period set in the previous Office action for reply and may result in abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If prosecution is not closed, amendments/replies will be entered and forwarded for consideration under 37 CFR 1.111. If under appeal and missing fee/submission, the application will be forwarded for appropriate treatment and applicant notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambiguous transmittal paper handling (CPA vs RCE)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a transmittal paper ambiguously references both CPA (37 CFR 1.53(d)) and RCE (37 CFR 1.114) for a plant or utility application filed on/after June 8, 1995, the Office will treat it as an RCE. If ambiguous for a design application, treat as CPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other papers filed with the transmittal (e.g., IDS or preliminary amendment) will not be considered in determining whether the transmittal is a CPA or RCE. Unambiguous RCE in a design application is an improper RCE and will be treated accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditional RCE treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: If submission is accompanied by a 'conditional' RCE and conditional payment authorization to charge deposit account, the Office will treat the conditional RCE and payment as if an RCE and payment of the fee had been filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mirrors treatment of conditional payments under other after-final/transitional fee provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry and ordering of amendments filed with RCE
rubrics_metrics.description: If RCE conditions are satisfied, previously filed unentered amendments and amendments filed with the RCE will normally be entered in the order filed unless applicant provides specific instructions for entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If conflicting amendments exist, applicant should clarify which to enter upon filing the RCE and is encouraged to file all amendments no later than the RCE filing to avoid disapproval of entry under 37 CFR 1.111(b). Consider filing a suspension of action if additional time is needed to prepare supplements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper CPA treated as RCE (post-July 14, 2003)
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant files a CPA on or after July 14, 2003 for a utility or plant application filed on/after June 8, 1995, the Office will automatically treat the improper CPA as an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the CPA does not satisfy RCE requirements (e.g., lacks submission or fee), it will be treated as an improper RCE and time in the last Office action will continue to run; expired time may require a petition under 37 CFR 1.137. Form paragraph 7.42.15 should be used to inform applicant that CPA is treated as RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-final RCE filing requirements and effect on finality
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant timely files an RCE with the 1.17(e) fee and a submission that meets the reply requirements of 37 CFR 1.111, the Office will withdraw the finality of any Office action to which a reply is outstanding and the submission will be entered and considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Merely requesting continued examination and paying the fee will not toll the running of any time period — the submission meeting 1.111 must be timely received. Use form paragraph 7.42.04.fti to notify applicant when finality is withdrawn after final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment format and marking requirements for after-final amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any submission that is an amendment must comply with the manner of making amendments as set forth in 37 CFR 1.121; the amendment must include markings showing changes relative to the last entered amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Previously filed unentered amendments after final may satisfy the submission requirement, but applicants are encouraged to file a consolidated amendment at the time of the RCE that incorporates desired changes and instructions regarding entry of earlier unentered amendments. See MPEP § 714.03 for amendment practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not fully responsive submissions — bona fide attempt requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If reply to a final Office action is outstanding and the submission is not fully responsive, it must be a bona fide attempt to provide a complete reply to the final Office action in order for the RCE to toll the period for reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not a bona fide attempt, treat as improper RCE and mail Form PTO-2051; the RCE will not toll the period and the application may be abandoned. Examples of non-bona fide submissions include an IDS-only submission or an amendment that cancels all claims without presenting new or substitute claims (such amendments will not be entered). See Exxon Corp. v. Phillips Petroleum Co., 265 F.3d 1249 (Fed. Cir. 2001).

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations considered bona fide attempts but not fully responsive
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain submissions may be bona fide attempts to provide a complete reply but are not fully responsive, e.g., non-compliant amendments or presentation of claims to a different invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-compliant amendments (not complying with 37 CFR 1.121) that are bona fide attempts, treat as proper RCE but mail a Notice of Noncompliant Amendment and give applicant two months to file a compliant amendment. If amendment presents only nonelected/independent claims (switching invention), treat RCE as proper but do not enter the amendment and give applicant two months to submit a complete reply. Use appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 7.42.08, 8.04, 8.26) and see MPEP § 821.03 for claim switching.
